The process condensate is recirculated through a direct cooling tower to remove heat. Residual particulates and other soluble components build up in the process condensate over time; to minimize the contaminants in the contact cooling water and avoid plugging concerns in the quench tower, a side stream is removed via blowdown. The overall purpose of this unit operation is to cool the shifted gas and remove the contaminants. Figure 1: PFD of Water Gas Shift Island 3.4 Process Description of WGS Island The WGS deploys high-temperature operations and offers flexibility on the extent of shift to optimize the calorific value of the H RF gas entering the powerhouse and the powerhouse performance. The WGS also 2 employs a low-pressure design to minimize the compressor capacity based on the pressure drops across the WGS reactors. BF gas enters the WGS battery limits with a volumetric flow rate of 429 MMSCFD (equivalent mass flow rate: 1,368 Klb/hr) at about atmospheric pressure (16.7 psia). The BF gas is compressed in 2 sets of centrifugal compressors up to 48.4 psia, to accommodate pressure drop across the system. An increase in pressure also favors the reaction kinetics in WGS reactors and lower reactor volume. This compressed gas would be pre-heated further via natural gas (NG) based feed preheater from 315°F to 767°F as per WGS reactor requirements. The pre-heater drops the gas pressure by four psia. The natural gas (NG) fired pre- heater consists of two convection banks & single radiant section to meet the temperature requirements. Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 7 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 The inlet temperature of the reactor is controlled by the flow of NG (as heater medium) to the feed gas pre- heater. The compressed & pre-heated BF gas is mixed with low-pressure (LP) steam before the reactor.
